svg.title: A CPU solves a batch one problem at a time, the Triton kernel solves it in parallel
svg.desc: Two lanes of eight small cost matrices. On the CPU a marker moves through them one by one. On the GPU all eight are scanned at the same time and finish together, long before the CPU lane.
svg.text: one problem at a time; each waits for the one before it
1. a CUDA batch is first copied from the GPU to the host
2. one core solves the problems in turn: the dashed outline is the one being solved, ✓ a finished one
3. only after the last problem are the assignments copied back to the GPU
one program per problem, all running at once; each step scans the columns as a vector
1. the batch stays on the GPU and one program starts for every problem
2. all programs scan the columns of their own matrix at once: the blue bar is that scan
3. all problems finish together, and nothing is copied to the host
Illustrative timing, not to scale: the measured speedups are in the benchmark tables below.
